oneLiner: 专制、民主与放任——勒温用实验让孩子体验：民主组质量更高，专制组更快却更脆。
oneLinerEn: Autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire — Lewin's experiments with children: democracy gave quality, autocracy speed but fragility.
detail: 库尔特·勒温 (1939) 把成年人带到后台，让同一批孩子分别由三种风格的“领导”带领做手工。专制组效率高但敌意与依赖强，领导一走就乱;民主组更有创造力与满意度，能自我维持;放任组最散漫、产出最低。风格没有绝对对错，但它确实塑造着群体的气氛与韧性。
detailEn: Kurt Lewin (1939) had adults lead the same children's arts group under three styles from behind a curtain. Autocratic clusters were productive but hostile and dependent — they fell apart when the leader left. Democratic ones showed more creativity and satisfaction and sustained themselves. Laissez-faire was the least productive. No style is universally right, but each shapes the group's climate and resilience.

oneLiner: 对新手多给指令，对专家多给授权——风格要随下属的能力与意愿切换。
oneLinerEn: Direct the novice, delegate to the expert — shift style with the follower's competence and commitment.
detail: 赫塞与布兰查德主张，有效的领导没有固定套路，只有四种模式沿“指令—教练—支持—授权”的光谱移动，随下属对特定任务的“成熟度”(能力 + 意愿)而选。同一位员工在不同任务上、在不同阶段，可能需要完全不同的对待。它直觉好用，但也因难以严格验证而受过学理批评。
detailEn: Hersey and Blanchard held there is no single right style, only four modes along a telling—selling—participating—delegating spectrum, chosen by the follower's readiness (competence plus commitment) for the specific task. The same person may need different handling across tasks and over time. Intuitively useful, it has been criticised as hard to validate rigorously.

oneLiner: 领导效能 = 领导风格 × 情境控制力的匹配度。
oneLinerEn: Leadership effectiveness is the match between a leader's style and the control the situation offers.
detail: 菲德勒用“最难共事同事(LPC)”量表衡量领导者是任务导向还是关系导向，再用上下级关系、任务结构、职位权力三项判断情境控制力。结论带有挑战性：任务导向者在极端有利或极端不利的处境表现更好，关系导向者在中间处境更好。而且他认为风格相对稳定，与其试图“改造人”，不如“把合适的人放到合适的岗位，或把情境改造成匹配领导”。
detailEn: Fiedler gauged whether a leader is task- or relationship-oriented with the 'Least Preferred Coworker' scale, then judged situational control from leader-member relations, task structure and position power. The conclusion was provocative: task leaders do best in situations either very favourable or very unfavourable, relationship leaders in the middle. And since he saw style as fairly fixed, he argued for matching the person to the situation — or reshaping the situation — rather than trying to rewire the person.

oneLiner: 交易型用奖惩交换绩效，变革型靠愿景、激发与关怀提升动机层次。
oneLinerEn: Transactional leaders trade rewards for performance; transformational ones raise motive through vision, stimulation and care.
detail: 伯恩斯奠基、巴斯发展：交易型领导明确“做到就给、做不到就罚”，在稳定任务中有效;变革型领导通过理想化的榜样、鼓舞人心的愿景、智力激发(鼓励质疑)与个性化关怀(因材施教)，把追随者从“为了报酬”推向“为了意义”。大量研究显示变革型与更高的绩效、承诺和满意度相关——但它需要真诚，否则易滑向作秀。
detailEn: Burns laid the groundwork, Bass developed it. Transactional leadership spells out 'deliver and be rewarded, fall short and be corrected' and works well on stable tasks. Transformational leadership uses idealised example, an inspiring vision, intellectual stimulation and individualised consideration to move followers from reward to meaning. Much research links it to higher performance, commitment and satisfaction — but it demands sincerity or it slides into theatre.

oneLiner: 生理、安全、归属、尊重、自我实现——未满足的低层需求主导行为。
oneLinerEn: Physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualisation: the lowest unsatisfied need drives behaviour.
detail: 亚伯拉罕·马斯洛 (1943) 把人的需求画成阶梯，主张低层相对满足后才向上追求。它对管理的启示很直接:饿着肚子或担心被裁的人，很难被“自我实现”的口号打动。它也常被批评:证据基础薄弱、分层过于刚性、带有西方个人主义色彩——把它当作提醒而非精确模型更稳妥。
detailEn: Abraham Maslow (1943) stacked human needs, holding that we pursue higher ones only once lower ones are relatively met. The managerial punch is blunt: people who are hungry or fearing the axe are not moved by appeals to self-actualisation. It is criticised for a thin evidence base, too-rigid tiers and a Western individualist slant — best used as a prompt, not a precise model.

oneLiner: 保健因素消除不满，激励因素带来满意——“满意”的反面不是“不满意”。
oneLinerEn: Hygiene removes dissatisfaction; motivators create satisfaction — the opposite of satisfaction is not dissatisfaction.
detail: 赫茨伯格访谈会计师与工程师后发现:薪资、政策、监督、条件等“保健因素”不足会让人不满，但把它们做好也只是“不再不满”，并不会真正点燃动力;真正带来满意与投入的是成就、认可、责任、成长与工作本身这些“激励因素”。这解释了为什么单纯加薪买不来长期敬业——它是止痛药，不是维生素。
detailEn: Interviewing accountants and engineers, Herzberg found that hygiene factors — pay, policy, supervision, conditions — when lacking breed dissatisfaction, but perfected only yield 'not dissatisfied', never true drive. Satisfaction and engagement come from motivators: achievement, recognition, the work itself, responsibility and growth. Hence a pay raise alone won't buy lasting engagement — it is a painkiller, not a vitamin.

term: 麦格雷戈 X-Y 理论
oneLiner: 你假设人惰性逃避(X)还是自主负责(Y)，制度与控制风格会被这个假设自我实现。
oneLinerEn: Assume people shirk (X) or own their work (Y), and your systems make that assumption come true.
detail: 道格拉斯·麦格雷戈 (1960) 指出:持 X 假设的管理者会搭严密的监控、惩罚与集权，恰恰把人逼得消极;持 Y 假设者会给自主、参与与成长，往往激发出责任感。它是“假设会自我实现”的经典表述。后续更谨慎的 Z 理论(威廉·大内)与情境观点提醒:人不是非 X 即 Y，管理方式要看任务、文化与个人。
detailEn: Douglas McGregor (1960) argued that managers who assume Theory X build tight surveillance, punishment and centralisation — which duly makes people passive; those who assume Theory Y grant autonomy, participation and growth, and often draw out ownership. It is a classic statement that assumptions self-fulfil. Later, more careful views — Theory Z (Ouchi) and contingency — remind us people are not simply X or Y and style must fit task, culture and person.

oneLiner: 动力 = 努力能达绩效 × 绩效能得报酬 × 报酬对我有价值；任一为零，激励归零。
oneLinerEn: Motivation = expectancy × instrumentality × valence; if any term is zero, motivation collapses.
detail: 维克托·弗鲁姆 (1964) 把激励拆成三个心理判断:我相信努力能换来好绩效吗(期望)?好绩效真会换来承诺的回报吗(工具性)?那回报是我想要的吗(效价)?这条链条把“为什么画大饼没用”讲得极清楚——只要员工不信、或奖励自己压根不在乎，激励力就乘成了零。管理者的抓手，就是逐环把这三问坐实。
detailEn: Victor Vroom (1964) decomposed motivation into three beliefs: will effort yield performance (expectancy), will performance yield the promised reward (instrumentality), and is that reward something I value (valence)? It states crisply why empty promises fail — if staff disbelieve any link, or do not want the prize, the product is zero. The manager's job is to make each link real.

oneLiner: 人会把自己的“得/付出”和参照对象比；一旦觉得亏待，就想办法把它扳平。
oneLinerEn: People compare their outcomes-to-inputs with a referent; feel shortchanged and they act to restore balance.
detail: 斯塔西·亚当斯认为公平是主观感知:你算出自己的“产出 ÷ 投入”，再与同事或同行比较，若感到被亏待，就会设法恢复平衡——少干活、要求加薪、在心里换一个参照对象，或者干脆离开。它对管理的启示是:绝对数额常常不如“相对公平感”重要;因此薪酬透明与程序公正(怎么决定的、可不可申诉)格外关键。
detailEn: J. Stacy Adams held that equity is a perception: you compute your outcomes over inputs, compare it with a colleague or market referent, and — feeling under-rewarded — act to restore balance: slack off, demand more, quietly switch referents, or leave. The lesson for managers is that relative fairness often matters more than absolute pay, so pay transparency and procedural justice (how a decision was made and can it be appealed) are crucial.

oneLiner: 具体而有挑战性、并配反馈的目标，比“尽力就好”更能提升绩效。
oneLinerEn: Specific, challenging goals with feedback beat 'do your best' at driving performance.
detail: 埃德温·洛克(与莱瑟姆)经过大量研究确立:目标通过四条途径起作用——引导注意、调动努力、延长坚持、激发策略探索。前提是员工接受了目标(承诺)、并有能力与反馈支撑。它也有阴暗面:为达成一个醒目数字而牺牲质量、走捷径甚至造假——所以目标要成组(兼顾质量与长期)，并把过程诚信与心理安全感一起设计进去。
detailEn: Edwin Locke (with Latham), across hundreds of studies, established that specific, challenging goals raise performance by directing attention, mobilising effort, sustaining persistence and sparking strategy — provided the person accepts the goal and has the ability and feedback to pursue it. It has a dark side: a lone salient number invites cut corners, quality damage or outright gaming. Hence goals should come in balanced sets, with process integrity and psychological safety designed alongside.
